catalog_quote: With a few exceptions, stress falls on the penultimate syllable. Examples (50) - (53) illustrate stress placement in non-suspect words. (50) a. /kalova/ [a'lova] tree ... (51) a. /manave-na/ [mana'wena] long ... (52) b. /a-kabi-i-di/ [axa'bidi] I took them ... Phonetically there are many words that appear not to follow the above stress pattern; instead of the stress falling on the penultimate syllable it falls on the antepenult. Examples of antepenultimate stress are given in the (a) examples below. The (b) examples show penultimate stress with suffixation. (54) a. /iaban/ ['yabana] heaven, sky b. /iaban-ia-na/ [yabani'ana] that heaven/sky ... However, if it is recognised that stress placement occurs after suffixation but before the epenthetic vowel [-a] is added (2.3.8), then all these examples are accounted for. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage, the exception passage and all three secondary locators are present verbatim in the held Olson 1992 text at the stated pages (268-269, 258, 313-314). (2) Deciding source: a 1992 Pacific Linguistics reference grammar sketch by the resident SIL fieldworker, the only published grammar of Gumawana per Glottolog; its stress section states penultimate stress with a derivational-ordering account of surface antepenults (C-final stems + epenthetic -a; -na neutralised inalienables) and an explicit closed exception list, which matches our rule string, prule, edge=right and exst=listed-set. (3) Better sources: none found.
